- When sentiment is positive (≥0.4) in recent days, model tends to underreact — adjust forecast upward by 0.5–1.5% relative to prior trend.
- When sentiment is negative (≤0.2) or volatile (e.g., 0.67, 1.00), model overestimates near-term recovery — reduce forecast slope or cap upward momentum.
- Model consistently underestimates true price drops after spikes (e.g., 85+ → 75–78) — apply downward bias of 2–5% for 3–5 day horizon post-spike.
- Model overestimates upward momentum after low points — apply mean reversion correction: if forecast > 1.5σ above recent mean, reduce by 0.5–1.0% per day.
- For 30-day horizon, model shows persistent bias toward flat or slightly rising trend — if true outcome shows sharp reversal, reduce forecast slope by 1–2% per day for 3–5 days.
- If sentiment history includes 1.00 (strong bullish), model often fails to capture subsequent crash — add 1–2 day lagged correction: reduce forecast by 1–3% on day after sentiment peak.
